successCriteria: I write a silent bar as a semibreve rest.
I write a silent beat as a dotted-crotchet rest, or a crotchet rest and a quaver rest.
I give each silent beat its own rest.

explanation.text: A bar that is completely silent is shown by a semibreve rest in every time signature you know. It hangs from the middle line, and it is not dotted, however long the bar is.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 6/8 with a semibreve rest.

explanation.caption: A silent bar: one semibreve rest.

explanation.text: A single silent beat of compound time can be written in two correct ways: one dotted-crotchet rest, or a crotchet rest followed by a quaver rest. Both mean exactly the same, and in this course both are accepted.

music.textAlternative: Two bars of 6/8: a dotted crotchet and a dotted-crotchet rest; then a dotted crotchet, a crotchet rest and a quaver rest.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: dotted crotchet, dotted crotchet rest. Bar 2: dotted crotchet, crotchet rest, quaver rest.

explanation.caption: Two ways to write one silent beat.

explanation.text: Give every silent beat its own rest, so the beats stay visible. Do not join two silent beats into one longer rest, and do not split a silent beat into three quaver rests.

In a bar of 12/8 there is one exception, as in 4/4: a rest may cover the first half of the bar (beats 1 and 2) or the second half (beats 3 and 4) as a single dotted-minim rest. It may not cover beats 2 and 3. A silent beat: one dotted-crotchet rest, or a crotchet rest and a quaver rest. Each silent beat gets its own rest.

music.textAlternative: A bar of 9/8: a beat of three quavers, a silent beat, then a dotted crotchet.

steps: Beat 2 is silent: write one dotted-crotchet rest for it.
Beat 3 is a dotted crotchet. Each beat has its own note or rest.

2.reason: Three separate quaver rests for one silent beat is too fussy. A silent beat is one dotted-crotchet rest, or a crotchet rest and a quaver rest.

3.reason: Within a silent beat the longer rest comes first: a crotchet rest then a quaver rest, or a single dotted-crotchet rest.

mistakes.beam-across-middle: In four-beat bars, keep the two halves of the bar visible — don't beam across the middle.
mistakes.rest-across-beat: That rest hides where a beat begins. Use one rest to finish the beat, and another for the next.
mistakes.half-bar-rest-misplaced: A two-beat rest can fill the first or second half of a four-beat bar, but not the middle two beats.
mistakes.tie-instead-of-dot: A dotted note says the same thing more simply here.
mistakes.compound-beat-hidden: In compound time each beat is a dotted note split into three. Group in threes so each beat shows.
mistakes.rest-grouping: A silent beat is one dotted-crotchet rest, or a crotchet rest and a quaver rest.

provenance.notes: Original wording. Follows Grade 3 outcome 2 (rests). OPEN_QUESTIONS Q4 (dotted rests in compound time): both accepted forms of a silent dotted-crotchet beat are taught and credited. Q25 (new): the half-bar dotted-minim rest of 12/8 is accepted, as the book allows. Partly silent beats (a note followed by a rest within one beat) are not asked, because the convention for them was not verified.
